items.stem: Define the term 'investment appraisal'.
items.answer: Evaluating the profitability or desirability of an investment project using quantitative methods (payback, ARR, NPV) and qualitative factors.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, evaluating the profitability or desirability of an investment project using quantitative methods (payback, ARR, NPV) and qualitative factors. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business might prefer a project with a shorter payback period.
items.answer: Cash is recovered sooner, reducing risk from uncertain future cash flows and improving liquidity; useful when technology changes fast.
items.markingKey: 1 mark lower risk; 1 mark liquidity/uncertainty. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one limitation of ARR.
items.answer: Advantage: uses all cash flows and gives a percentage that can be compared with interest rates or targets. Limitation: ignores timing of cash flows / time value of money.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each with explanation. [2]

items.stem: BatikPay Sdn Bhd is a private limited company based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops and employs about 210 people. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain why BatikPay might reject a project with a high ARR.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: ARR averages profit over the life; long payback increases risk; cash flows uncertain in later years; qualitative factors or better alternatives.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: ARR averages profit over the life. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for BatikPay, e.g. long payback increases risk; cash flows uncertain in later years; qualitative factors or better alternatives. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is a private limited company based in Nairobi, Kenya. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe and employs about 850 people. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Discuss whether quantitative investment appraisal is enough for Savanna Fresh to decide whether to invest.
items.answer: For: objective comparison; shows financial return; helps raise finance. Against: based on forecasts; ignores qualitative factors (staff, image, strategy); risk not fully captured. Judgement: the decision for Savanna Fresh depends mainly on the reliability of forecasts, and also on strategic importance of the project.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Savanna Fresh: horticulture, about 850 employees, private limited company in Kenya; its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. objective comparison; shows financial return; helps raise finance; arguments against, e.g. based on forecasts; ignores qualitative factors (staff, image, strategy); risk not fully captured. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the reliability of forecasts; strategic importance of the project; stakeholder impacts. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Savanna Fresh, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which is a main advantage of the payback method?
options: It measures profitability as a percentage
It considers all cash flows over the project's life
It takes account of the time value of money
It is simple and highlights how quickly the investment is recovered, reducing risk
items.answer: It is simple and highlights how quickly the investment is recovered, reducing risk
items.markingKey: It is simple and highlights how quickly the investment is recovered, reducing risk. Payback is easy and focuses on liquidity and risk.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'investment appraisal'?
options: Reducing the value of future cash flows to give their present value, because money received in the future is worth less than money received today.
The idea that a sum of money is worth more now than the same sum in the future, because it could be invested to earn interest.
Evaluating the profitability or desirability of an investment project using quantitative methods (payback, ARR, NPV) and qualitative factors.
The average annual profit from an investment expressed as a percentage of its initial cost: (total net profit ÷ years) ÷ initial cost × 100.
items.answer: Evaluating the profitability or desirability of an investment project using quantitative methods (payback, ARR, NPV) and qualitative factors.
items.markingKey: investment appraisal: Evaluating the profitability or desirability of an investment project using quantitative methods (payback, ARR, NPV) and qualitative factors.

items.stem: Explain why the results of investment appraisal are uncertain.
items.answer: They rely on forecasts of costs and revenues several years ahead, which may be wrong because of economic change, competition or technology.
items.markingKey: 1 mark forecasts; 1 mark reasons for error. [2]

items.stem: Deccan Auto Components Ltd is considering investing $500,000 in components for electric vehicles. Forecast net cash inflows are: year 1 $118,000, year 2 $178,000, year 3 $217,000, year 4 $237,000. Calculate the payback period.
items.answer: Payback 2 years 11 months
items.markingKey: Cumulative after 2 years = $296,000; remaining $204,000 recovered in $204,000/$217,000 × 12 = 11 months [1]; payback = 2 years 11 months [1]. [2]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is considering investing $100,000 in serviced apartments for long-stay guests. Forecast net cash inflows are: year 1 $25,000, year 2 $38,000, year 3 $46,000, year 4 $51,000. Calculate the payback period and the average rate of return.
items.answer: Payback 2 years 10 months; ARR 15%
items.markingKey: Cumulative after 2 years = $63,000; remaining $37,000 recovered in $37,000/$46,000 × 12 = 10 months [1]; payback = 2 years 10 months [1]; total profit = $160,000 − $100,000 = $60,000 [1]; average annual profit = $15,000 [1]; ARR = 15% [1]. [5]

items.stem: Define the term 'net present value (NPV)'.
items.answer: The total present value of a project's future net cash flows minus the initial cost of the investment.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, the total present value of a project's future net cash flows minus the initial cost of the investment. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why NPV is often considered better than payback for appraising investments.
items.answer: NPV uses all cash flows over the project's life and allows for the time value of money, so it measures the true increase in value, not just speed of repayment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark all cash flows; 1 mark time value of money. [2]

items.stem: Explain how the choice of discount rate affects investment decisions.
items.answer: A higher rate reduces present values, so fewer projects have positive NPVs; the rate should reflect the cost of finance and risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark effect on PV/NPV; 1 mark link to cost of capital/risk. [2]

Explain why Cape Brew should use discounted cash flow methods when appraising long-term projects.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: DCF allows for the time value of money; later cash flows are worth less in present value terms; discount rate can reflect cost of capital and risk; NPV shows value created.

items.stem: A project has a positive NPV at a discount rate of 10%. This means
options: its payback is less than one year
its ARR is exactly 10%
its discounted cash inflows exceed the initial cost
it will definitely be profitable
items.answer: its discounted cash inflows exceed the initial cost
items.markingKey: its discounted cash inflows exceed the initial cost. Positive NPV: the project earns more than the 10% cost of capital, if forecasts are correct.

items.stem: Define the term 'sensitivity analysis'.
items.answer: Testing how the outcome of an investment appraisal changes if key forecasts (e.g. sales, costs, discount rate) turn out differently.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, testing how the outcome of an investment appraisal changes if key forecasts (e.g. sales, costs, discount rate) turn out differently. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why managers should consider qualitative factors in investment decisions.
items.answer: Numbers cannot capture effects on morale, reputation, the environment or strategic fit, which may decide long-run success.
items.markingKey: 1 mark examples; 1 mark long-run impact. [2]

items.stem: Explain how sensitivity analysis helps managers deal with risk.
items.answer: It shows how much the forecasts can change before the project becomes unviable, so managers can judge how safe the margin is.
items.markingKey: 1 mark testing assumptions; 1 mark judging margin of safety. [2]
